CT420 Revision

Protocol Analysis Tools

Turn a capture or trace into evidence, not a screenshot tour.

Rapid exam refresher

  • Wireshark packets, encrypted QUIC limit.
  • qlog endpoint events, qVis visualises.
  • waterfall critical path.
  • correlate clocks.

Purpose, scope and examiner demand

Wireshark, qlog and qvis/qViz help diagnose protocol timing and behaviour. In exams, state what you would measure, how you would filter/visualise it, and the conclusion it can support.

Exam focus by part

  • Wireshark packets, encrypted QUIC limit.
  • qlog endpoint events, qVis visualises.
  • waterfall critical path.
  • correlate clocks.

Question-demand diagnosis and answer plan

  1. Translate the symptom into observables: handshake timing, retransmissions, stream progress, loss, RTT, or throughput.
  2. Choose capture/trace source and scope it to the affected flow.
  3. Describe a filter, graph or event sequence.
  4. Give a bounded conclusion and name a measurement limitation.

Question-type cues

  • Application cue: Diagnose QUIC stream stalls.
  • Analysis cue: Waterfall shows long wait.

Definitions, notation and discriminating comparisons

  • Packet capture (PCAP): recorded packets; display filter: narrows what is shown without changing capture data.
  • qlog: structured QUIC event log; qvis/qViz: visualises QUIC traces.
  • RTT: round-trip time; retransmission/loss: evidence of recovery or missing delivery, not automatically the root cause.
  • Goodput: useful delivered application data per time, distinct from raw link rate.

Step-by-step methods and solution routes

A page is slow only on one network. Capture the client flow, isolate the connection, and place handshake, request and response events on a timeline. If setup is fast but gaps follow loss/recovery events, inspect RTT and stream progress in qlog/qViz. Compare with a known-good run. Conclude "consistent with loss/recovery delay" rather than claiming a router fault without corroboration.

Reasoning checkpoints

  1. Use and justify: Wireshark packets, encrypted QUIC limit.
  2. Use and justify: qlog endpoint events, qVis visualises.
  3. Use and justify: waterfall critical path.
  4. Use and justify: correlate clocks.

Worked examples and method extensions

Question

How would you investigate a suspected QUIC stream stall?

Model answer

Collect a qlog and, where permitted, a packet capture for the affected connection. Use qViz to inspect stream events, packet loss/recovery and RTT over time. Correlate the period where the application stalled with stream delivery and congestion events, then compare a normal trace. The trace can show correlation and protocol behaviour; encryption, clock alignment and missing server-side data can limit diagnosis.

Exam-paper-led practice

Practice question 1 [medium/hard]

Scenario and demand: A QUIC video stream stalls while other streams continue. Specify an evidence plan using packet capture, qlog and qvis. [9 marks]

Question-demand diagnosis and fastest route: Wireshark can show UDP/QUIC packet timing and transport symptoms but encryption limits application/stream interpretation without keys. Collect endpoint qlog events for stream state, packet loss, congestion window and recovery; load them into qvis to correlate timelines and identify whether the stalled stream is flow-control, server scheduling or loss recovery. Align host clocks and preserve trace IDs. Trap: a waterfall alone cannot reveal encrypted endpoint scheduling decisions.

Practice question 2 [medium/hard]

Scenario and demand: A web waterfall shows 900 ms “waiting” before a critical CSS response. Give a falsifiable diagnosis path. [8 marks]

Question-demand diagnosis and fastest route: Separate DNS/connect/TLS/request/TTFB/content phases and correlate browser waterfall with server timing, qlog and packet trace. Long waiting/TTFB suggests queueing, server work or upstream dependency rather than slow download; test cache hit/miss, backend spans and request priority. State the result only after the timings agree. Trap: blaming bandwidth when the bytes transfer quickly after first response.

Verified local-paper basis

Verified families: 2023/24 Q5(a–b) and 2024/25 Q5(a–b) (Wireshark, qlog/qViz and waterfalls).

Topic-specific traps and diagnosis

  • Reading a single packet as proof of the root cause.
  • Confusing capture-time clock with remote endpoint time.
  • Ignoring encryption, sampling, or missing trace context.

Exam marking checklist

  • What exact symptom and metric am I testing?
  • What evidence would refute my hypothesis?
  • Have I stated a limitation?

Paper-years note

Wireshark/qLog/qViz and web-performance analysis belong mainly to the recent direction noted for 2023/24-2024/25. Tool names may change, so learn the diagnostic reasoning as well as the interface.

Practice-source note

The added questions synthesise recurring local CT420 paper patterns: scheduling calculations, time synchronisation, priority protocols, QUIC analysis, QoS and fault tolerance. They are not presented as exact wording from a named year.
